panels.prompt: A stylized historical document showing the arXiv preprint page of a famous research paper, slightly yellowed parchment feel like a founding charter, the title 'Attention Is All You Need' in large bold serif type at the top, eight author names listed beneath in smaller text, the date 'Submitted on 12 Jun 2017' visible, the Google Brain and Google Research logos faintly visible, mathematical notation and diagram fragments visible on the page, solemn and historic atmosphere like viewing an important manuscript, Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, warm sepia and cream tones with blue #4A9BD9 title accent

panels.text: Eight authors. Twelve pages. One audacious claim: you could throw away the entire recurrent framework and replace it with a single mechanism -- attention alone. They called the architecture the Transformer.

A white speech bubble with black outline near the top. Inside the bubble the text reads: "They titled the paper like a mic drop." panels.caption: The Transformer beat previous translation models in quality AND training speed.

panels.prompt: A packed conference hall at NeurIPS 2017 in Long Beach California, hundreds of researchers filling every seat and standing along the walls, the Transformer architecture diagram projected on a massive screen at the front, warm stage lighting illuminating the presenter, the audience leaning forward with intense interest, cameras and laptops everywhere, the atmosphere is charged with excitement, Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, warm amber stage light with blue #4A9BD9 diagram on screen

panels.text: The speed improvement was even more dramatic. Because every word could attend to every other word simultaneously, the entire computation could be spread across GPU cores in parallel. No more waiting for word five to finish before starting word six.

panels.text: The Transformer paper was written to solve machine translation. Its authors did not set out to create the foundation of ChatGPT, Claude, or the entire modern AI industry. But the architecture was so powerful and so general that it became exactly that. Great inventions often outgrow their inventors' intentions.
The Transformer worked. But what was it, exactly? How does "attention" actually function? Time to open the hood.
